facts.text: Construction approved 1947, begun winter 1948, cornerstone laid Nov 11, 1949, dedicated Oct 14, 1950.
Named for Albert Kingsbury, UNH's first mechanical engineering professor, who invented the thrust bearing in Durham in 1898.
Phase 1 of the $52.98M renovation finished January 2006 with a new 45,000 sq ft wing devoted to labs.
Labs have large windows on both sides so passers-by can see work in progress; two lecture halls and student project spaces.
Fire suppression sprinklers were installed in Kingsbury in years before 2025.

verdict: Engineering's big 1950 block with a 2006 metal-and-glass lab wing; institutional outside, full of daylit study nooks students like.
notes: Photos (2013) show a large complex: red-brick wings with banded windows, a glazed stair tower, and a grey metal-panel wing with ribbon windows; neat but institutional. Strong daylight in lounges per Her Campus. Old row's "HVAC/air conditioning throughout" not confirmed on an opened page (CEPS page only says labs have appropriate infrastructure). UNH Magazine says Phase 2 "will renovate" the 55-year-old building; completion 2007 per old row and search excerpts, not re-opened. Renovation architect not found. Admissions blog posts are UNH-run.
judgeNotes: Photos show neat but heterogeneous wings. Reputation up a point for consistently positive student comments.
